title: Germany 30-Year Bund multi-ISIN auction (EUR 2.5bn across two reopening lines) — the year's last long-end auction, on the one day the US bond market is shut
source: EST: deutsche-finanzagentur.de English issuance calendar (/en/federal-securities/issuances/issuance-calendar), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 124,976 bytes) — the Quarter IV 2026 table lists TWO 30-year reopening lines dated 11.11.2026, 'Bund 30 Y (R)' at EUR 1.5bn and 'Bund 30 Y (R)' at EUR 1.0bn, both with ISIN, coupon and maturity shown as '-'. CORROBORATED BY TWO FURTHER FINANZAGENTUR PRIMARIES, both fetched direct this session and both published months earlier. (1) The H2 2026 issuance outlook workbook (Issuance_outlook_2026_Update_Q3_en.xlsx, HTTP 200, 78,201 bytes, 'As of June 2026') carries a single row for 2026-11-11 reading 'Bund | 30 years | Reopenings (multi-ISIN) | 2500' with NO accompanying '15/20/30 years' flexible line — the same full-30Y commitment 10-14 carries and unlike 09-16, which pairs '30 years | 1500' with a flexible '15/20/30 years | 1000'. (2) THE ANNUAL ISSUANCE PLAN ITSELF, Press Release No. 10 of 18 December 2025 (2025_12_18_pm_10_Emissionsplanung_Bund_2026_en.pdf, HTTP 200, 435,446 bytes), whose text states verbatim: 'For outstanding 30-year Federal bonds, an auction date is scheduled each month except December. A total volume of EUR 29.0 billion will be placed via these eleven taps... In January, April and July, EUR 3.0 billion will be issued via up to three different Federal bonds in one auction date. In the remaining months, up to two bonds with a volume of EUR 2.5 billion are planned.' Its Annex monthly row for Bund (30 years) reads 3.0 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 3.0 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 3.0 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 2.5 across January-November and NOTHING for December, summing to exactly EUR 29.0bn. So November's EUR 2.5bn two-line shape was announced eleven months ahead, and the absence of a December date is stated policy rather than a calendar reading. 11.11.2026 is a Wednesday, the day Germany auctions nominal Bunds of 7 years or more; the auction-process page (HTTP 200, 96,556 bytes) puts the announcement four bank business days ahead, i.e. 2026-11-05, with the second bond 'only announced in a press notice in the week before the auction'. The Finanzagentur press index's newest notice on 2026-09-09 is dated September 09, 2026 — nothing for 11-11 yet, as expected at D-63. Filed estimate on the same mechanical count as both siblings: market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed source prefix for a non-US sovereign debt office, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Proposed during the bund-30y-auction-2026-10-14 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-09) and researched the same day (docs/research/events/bund-30y-auction-2026-11-11.md); this canonical file replaces the proposal it arrived as. Germany sells EUR 2.5bn of 30-year duration with bidding closing 11:30 CET (10:30 UTC = 05:30 ET). Tiered `low` and NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: no house playbook is rates-keyed and no tracked symbol carries euro-rates exposure. FOUR FINDINGS ARE NEW TO THIS LEDGER, and the first changes what the entry can measure at all. (1) THE US BOND MARKET IS SHUT ON 2026-11-11 (Veterans Day, sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-11-11), so THE SAME-DATE TRANSATLANTIC TEST BOTH SIBLINGS RAN IS UNDEFINED HERE — proven mechanically from Treasury's own primary rather than from a holiday calendar: across 1999-2026 the daily par yield curve has published a reading on November 11 exactly ZERO times, including all 14 weekday instances. The Bundesbank quotes the Bund 30Y on 18 of those, so Germany trades and the US does not. (2) THE T+1 TEST, THE ONLY TRANSATLANTIC TEST THAT EXISTS FOR THIS DATE, IS ALSO A NULL — soft-vs-firm bid-to-offer moves the next US session's 30Y CMT +0.19bp (SE 0.65, t = 0.29, n = 104/102) and undersubscribed-vs-covered -0.36bp (t = -0.54). Its naive version returns a spurious t = 2.19 because `next US session` jumps the CMT's 1,455-day hole; the guard is load-bearing. (3) A MISATTRIBUTION IN THE SIBLING IS CORRECTED: the 9 auction dates with no same-date US CMT reading are 7 inside that hole plus TWO GENUINE US BOND HOLIDAYS — 2020-11-11 (Veterans Day, the exact structural precedent, n = 1) and 2024-06-19 (Juneteenth). (4) 'NO DECEMBER 30Y DATE' IS NEITHER A CUT NOR A NOVELTY: the debt office pre-announced 'each month except December' in December 2025, and Germany has auctioned a 30-year Bund in December ZERO times in 218 auction-process dates since 1999 — which retires the December limb of FT-bund-30y-auction-2026-10-14-4 as dead on arrival. The core spillover null replicates exactly on an independently rebuilt pipeline (213 dates, median bid-to-offer 1.3230, 47 undersubscribed = 22.1%, same-date US 30Y -0.04bp/t = -0.06, Bund 30Y +0.35bp/t = 0.66, allotment band mean EUR 2,001m sd 105 on 23 identical-shape dates). Adjacency is the densest of the three: 11-11 sits INSIDE the US November refunding week — treasury-3y-note-2026-11-09, treasury-10y-note-2026-11-10 and jgb-30y-auction-2026-11-10 before it, treasury-30y-bond-2026-11-12 the very next day — so unlike 10-14 this IS a synchronised global long-end block, and Germany gets the one session with no US competition because the US bond market is closed. cpi-2026-11-10 (confirmed, high) and us-china-tariff-truce-expiry-2026-11-10 land the day before. One trap follows mechanically: the US 30Y's first session after a bond holiday moves 4.84bp vs 4.03bp normally (t = 2.74, n = 169, 1.20x), because that print spans two calendar days — so 11-12's US long-end move is arithmetically inflated AND carries the US 30Y auction result, and must never be read as Bund-auction spillover. The 04.11.2026 Bund 15Y pair on the same Q4 calendar is recorded and not filed: wrong tenor for this ledger's question, the same call both siblings made. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
